osps_ac_01_01_justification: Two-factor authentication is required organisation-wide: GitHub reports two_factor_requirement_enabled for the monumental-archive organisation, covering repository write access and private vulnerability reports alike.
osps_ac_02_01_justification: Collaborator permissions are assigned explicitly, never inherited by default. The repository baseline script sets the default repository permission to the lowest privilege and review routing goes through CODEOWNERS to the `owners` team; the settings are code, applied and drift-checked by settings/repo-baseline.sh. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/tree/main/settings
osps_ac_03_01_justification: An organisation-level ruleset blocks direct pushes to main: every change must arrive as a pull request and pass required status checks. The rules and their rationale are recorded in docs/rulesets.md and the Monday audit re-checks them for drift. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/docs/rulesets.md
osps_ac_03_02_justification: The organisation ruleset restricts branch deletion on the primary branch, so deleting main is refused rather than confirmed away. Recorded in docs/rulesets.md. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/docs/rulesets.md
osps_ac_04_01_justification: Least privilege is the default and the explicit setting: the repository baseline sets the workflow token to read-only permissions, and every workflow declares its own minimal `permissions:` block on top of that. A job that specifies nothing therefore gets read, not write. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/tree/main/settings
osps_ac_04_02_justification: Every workflow declares an explicit `permissions:` block scoped to what that job actually needs, on top of a read-only default set by the repository baseline. The strongest case is enforced by a lint: no workflow that runs caller-supplied code may hold `id-token: write`, and lint:capability-boundary fails the build if one ever does.
osps_br_01_01_justification: This repository's workflows are callers of the org's shared workflows, which validate their inputs against allowlists (the artifact `classes:` input, the release-stub shape checked by lint:release-stub); zizmor fails the gate on template-injection patterns where untrusted context would reach a shell.
osps_br_01_03_justification: Org-level control: no shared workflow that runs caller-supplied code may declare `id-token: write`, enforced by lint:capability-boundary. In this repository only publish.yml and release.yml grant id-token, and the image is signed by the separate org signer, not by a job that runs this repository's build code. https://github.com/monumental-archive/iiif-server/blob/main/.github/workflows/publish.yml
osps_br_01_04_justification: Collaborator-supplied input to the CI/CD pipeline is validated by the shared workflows (allowlisted inputs, release-stub shape) and zizmor fails the gate on untrusted-context interpolation.
osps_br_02_01_justification: Every release carries a unique semantic version: the workspace version in Cargo.toml (0.2.3 today) and an immutable v-prefixed tag minted by the org release workflow that .github/workflows/release.yml calls. Tags are never reused; MAINTENANCE.md 'What a version number promises' states that version tags are immutable. https://github.com/monumental-archive/iiif-server/blob/main/MAINTENANCE.md
osps_br_02_02_justification: Verified on the published release v0.2.3: every asset is named for the release (iiif-server-0.2.3.spdx.json, iiif-server-0.2.3-image.spdx.json, sbom-image-iiif-server-0.2.3.spdx.json) and each is bound by digest in checksums.txt and in the attestations.intoto.jsonl evidence bundle; the container image is tagged v0.2.3 in GHCR and attested by digest. https://github.com/monumental-archive/iiif-server/releases/tag/v0.2.3
osps_br_03_01_justification: Every official channel is HTTPS: the repository, releases, documentation and issue tracker are all served by GitHub over TLS, and no plaintext URI appears in the tree.
osps_br_03_02_justification: The distributed artifact is the container image, served by GHCR over HTTPS and authenticated beyond transport: it is signed keylessly with build provenance, and docs/deployment.md 'Verifying what you pulled' gives the `gh attestation verify` command that checks the signer identity and source ref. Release assets are bound by digest in checksums.txt and attestations.intoto.jsonl. https://github.com/monumental-archive/iiif-server/blob/main/docs/deployment.md#verifying-what-you-pulled
osps_br_04_01_justification: CHANGELOG.md records each release's functional and security changes, generated from conventional commits by the org release workflow, and the same notes are attached to each GitHub release (v0.2.3 lists its fixes, the [security] dependency updates and the build changes). https://github.com/monumental-archive/iiif-server/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md
osps_br_05_01_justification: Dependencies are ingested through cargo from crates.io only, against the committed Cargo.lock with --locked; deny.toml denies unknown registries and git sources. Toolchains come through mise with mise.lock checksums. https://github.com/monumental-archive/iiif-server/blob/main/deny.toml
osps_br_06_01_justification: Each release carries a Sigstore evidence bundle (attestations.intoto.jsonl) and checksums.txt covering every asset, and the image is signed with build provenance by the org signer. docs/deployment.md documents verifying it. https://github.com/monumental-archive/iiif-server/releases/tag/v0.2.3
osps_br_07_01_justification: Secret scanning with push protection is enforced by the organisation security configuration, so an unencrypted credential is blocked at push time; trivy's secret rules also run in the gate. The architecture removes most of the risk at source: publishing is keyless via OIDC and trusted publishing, so there are few long-lived secrets to leak.
osps_br_07_02_justification: docs/continuity.md is the secrets policy in operational form: an asset table naming every credential the project uses, where it is stored, who can reach it, and how it is rotated or recreated — including the one standing token, whose expiry is designed to fail loudly rather than silently under-claim. The policy is short because the architecture removes most secrets: publishing is keyless via OIDC and trusted publishing, and no signing key exists to store. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/docs/continuity.md
osps_do_01_01_justification: README.md covers basic use: the `docker run` and `serve s3://` invocations, what ships, and configuration; docs/deployment.md covers running, verifying, TLS, caching and access control. https://github.com/monumental-archive/iiif-server/blob/main/README.md
osps_do_02_01_justification: SUPPORT.md and the repository's issue forms document how to report a defect, and SECURITY.md documents the separate private path for vulnerabilities. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/SUPPORT.md
osps_do_03_01_justification: docs/deployment.md 'Verifying what you pulled' gives the `gh attestation verify` command a consumer runs to check the image's integrity and provenance. https://github.com/monumental-archive/iiif-server/blob/main/docs/deployment.md#verifying-what-you-pulled
osps_do_03_02_justification: The same section states the expected author identity: the signer's workflow (monumental-archive/signer/.github/workflows/sign.yml), passed as --signer-workflow, with the source ref. https://github.com/monumental-archive/iiif-server/blob/main/docs/deployment.md#verifying-what-you-pulled
osps_do_04_01_justification: The org SECURITY.md (served to this repository, which carries no copy) states support scope and duration: only the latest release receives security fixes, by rolling forward. MAINTENANCE.md adds this repository's response window: advisories triaged within 7 days and released as signed patch releases. https://github.com/monumental-archive/iiif-server/blob/main/MAINTENANCE.md
osps_do_05_01_justification: The org SECURITY.md states that a release stops receiving security updates when the next release exists; MAINTENANCE.md states the tag policy (immutable versions, floating 0.x tags). https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/SECURITY.md
osps_do_06_01_justification: docs/design-spec.md 'Dependency doctrine' states how dependencies are selected (pure Rust where untrusted bytes are parsed, permissive licences, the tracked class), deny.toml enforces licences, sources and bans, and Renovate (renovate.json) records how they are updated. https://github.com/monumental-archive/iiif-server/blob/main/docs/design-spec.md
osps_do_07_01_justification: README.md 'Building and developing': `mise install && mise run hooks:install` brings the pinned Rust toolchains and tools from the lockfile; `mise run ci` builds and tests. MSRV is stated (Rust 1.96). https://github.com/monumental-archive/iiif-server/blob/main/README.md
osps_gv_01_01_justification: docs/continuity.md carries an asset table naming who holds each sensitive resource — organisation ownership, the tag-mint App key, registry accounts, the one standing token — and what happens to each if that person is unavailable. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/docs/continuity.md
osps_gv_01_02_justification: GOVERNANCE.md carries a 'Roles and responsibilities' table naming three roles - maintainer/owner, contributor, automation - and the responsibilities of each, and it is served from the organisation's .github repository as a default community health file so it applies to every repository that does not carry its own. Who holds the maintainer role is explicit: the @monumental-archive/owners team, which CODEOWNERS routes every review to. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md#roles-and-responsibilities
osps_gv_02_01_justification: GitHub Issues and pull requests are public and open for discussion of changes and usage obstacles. https://github.com/monumental-archive/iiif-server/issues
osps_gv_03_01_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md explains the contribution process: open an issue first for anything large, pull requests for small self-contained fixes, Conventional Commits, DCO sign-off, a green `mise run ci`, squash merge. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
osps_gv_03_02_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md includes a 'Requirements for acceptable contributions' section: pull request only, a green `mise run ci`, Conventional Commits with imperative lowercase subjects under 72 columns, DCO sign-off, squash merge. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
osps_gv_04_01_justification: GOVERNANCE.md section 'Escalation and permissions' carries the policy: a collaborator is reviewed before being granted any escalated permission. Concretely, before an account joins @monumental-archive/owners or receives write access anywhere, the maintainer reviews who they are, why the access is needed and what the smallest sufficient grant is - and the grant is then recorded in the settings-as-code baseline so drift is auditable. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md#escalation-and-permissions
osps_le_01_01_justification: Every commit must carry a Developer Certificate of Origin 1.1 sign-off asserting legal authorisation. The commit-msg hook catches a missing trailer locally and lint:dco fails the gate, with no exemption list — automation signs off too.
osps_le_02_02_justification: The released image carries the same AGPL-3.0-only licence as the source; the SPDX SBOMs on each release record it. https://github.com/monumental-archive/iiif-server/blob/main/LICENSE
osps_le_03_01_justification: LICENSE at the repository root and LICENSES/AGPL-3.0-only.txt in the REUSE location; api.reuse.software reports the repository compliant. https://github.com/monumental-archive/iiif-server/blob/main/LICENSE
osps_le_03_02_justification: Release assets are published from this repository, which carries LICENSE and LICENSES/AGPL-3.0-only.txt; the source SBOM on each release names the licence. https://github.com/monumental-archive/iiif-server/blob/main/LICENSE
osps_qa_01_01_justification: Publicly readable at a static URL. https://github.com/monumental-archive/iiif-server
osps_qa_01_02_justification: Git records what changed, who changed it and when, for every revision, and the history is public. Beyond that, each revision carries a signed source-provenance attestation, so the record is independently verifiable rather than merely readable.
osps_qa_02_01_justification: Cargo.toml lists every direct dependency and Cargo.lock pins the full tree with checksums; mise.toml and mise.lock do the same for toolchains. https://github.com/monumental-archive/iiif-server/blob/main/Cargo.toml
osps_qa_02_02_justification: Every release ships SPDX SBOMs as release assets, generated by the release pipeline rather than hand-kept. Verified on v0.2.3: iiif-server-0.2.3.spdx.json (source), iiif-server-0.2.3-image.spdx.json and sbom-image-iiif-server-0.2.3.spdx.json (image). The binary is built with cargo-auditable (mise.toml) so the dependency tree is also embedded in the shipped executable. https://github.com/monumental-archive/iiif-server/releases/tag/v0.2.3
osps_qa_03_01_justification: The gate is a required status check on main under an organisation ruleset: a pull request cannot merge red, and direct pushes are blocked entirely, so no commit reaches the primary branch without its checks passing. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/docs/rulesets.md
osps_qa_04_01_justification: The codebases are listed: the workspace members in Cargo.toml (crates/core, crates/sources, crates/server) described in CLAUDE.md 'Architecture', and the separate, unreleased fuzz workspace (fuzz/). https://github.com/monumental-archive/iiif-server/blob/main/Cargo.toml
osps_qa_04_02_justification: A release is this single repository's container image; the workspace crates are publish = false and released only inside it, so there are no additional subprojects released alongside it.
osps_qa_05_01_justification: No generated executable artifacts are committed; the binary is built in the release pipeline. The only binary files tracked are test images under tests/fixtures, which are inputs, not executables. https://github.com/monumental-archive/iiif-server/tree/main/tests/fixtures
osps_qa_05_02_justification: The only binary files are small test images in tests/fixtures, each pinned by digest in tests/fixtures/SHA256SUMS; larger masters are generated by scripts/gen_fixtures.sh rather than committed. https://github.com/monumental-archive/iiif-server/blob/main/tests/fixtures/SHA256SUMS
osps_qa_06_01_justification: .github/workflows/ci.yml runs the full gate, tests included, on every pull request as a required check before it can merge. https://github.com/monumental-archive/iiif-server/blob/main/.github/workflows/ci.yml
osps_qa_06_02_justification: README.md states that `mise run ci` locally is exactly what CI runs, and CLAUDE.md 'Commands' lists when each check runs: the gate on every pull request and push to main, the fuzz and validator audits on the Monday cron. https://github.com/monumental-archive/iiif-server/blob/main/README.md
osps_qa_06_03_justification: Org CONTRIBUTING.md item 3 (served to this repository) requires new behaviour to add the check that holds it and bug fixes to add the reproducing case; CLAUDE.md adds that correctness fixes want a failing test first. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
osps_qa_07_01_justification: With a single maintainer there is no non-author human approval available, so this is not enforced. It is the headcount wall this project records rather than works around: the same boundary as Gold's two_person_review and SLSA Source L4, tracked as an open issue rather than quietly claimed. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/docs/slsa-reference.md
osps_sa_01_01_justification: docs/design-spec.md is the design, CLAUDE.md 'Architecture' maps the crates, and docs/assurance-case.md 'Trust boundaries' names the actors and data flows (clients, the server, masters on disk or in an object store); docs/release-engineering.md covers the release actors. https://github.com/monumental-archive/iiif-server/blob/main/docs/assurance-case.md
osps_sa_02_01_justification: The external interfaces are the IIIF Image API endpoints, /healthz, /metrics and the CLI; README.md and docs/deployment.md document them and MAINTENANCE.md states which are covered by semver. https://github.com/monumental-archive/iiif-server/blob/main/README.md
osps_sa_03_01_justification: docs/assurance-case.md is the security assessment: threat model, trust boundaries, the common weaknesses and how each is countered, and what remains. https://github.com/monumental-archive/iiif-server/blob/main/docs/assurance-case.md
osps_sa_03_02_justification: docs/assurance-case.md 'Threat model' and 'Trust boundaries' are the threat model and attack-surface analysis: hostile URLs and hostile master bytes as the critical paths, each with its control. https://github.com/monumental-archive/iiif-server/blob/main/docs/assurance-case.md
osps_vm_01_01_justification: SECURITY.md is the coordinated disclosure policy and it states the timeframe: private reporting through the repository's Security tab, acknowledgement within 14 days, and what the reporter can expect afterwards. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/SECURITY.md
osps_vm_02_01_justification: SECURITY.md names the security contact and the reporting channel: private vulnerability reporting through the repository's Security tab, with a 14-day acknowledgement commitment. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/SECURITY.md
osps_vm_03_01_justification: GitHub private vulnerability reporting is enabled and is the documented channel in SECURITY.md, delivering the report directly to the security contact without public exposure. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/SECURITY.md
osps_vm_04_01_justification: Vulnerability data would be published as GitHub Security Advisories on this repository; none has been published because none has been found in the project's own code. Dependency advisory decisions are made in the release path and Renovate's security updates. https://github.com/monumental-archive/iiif-server/security/advisories
osps_vm_04_02_justification: Exactly this: the dependency track emits VEX documents keyed by package@version recording non-exploitability decisions for advisories that do not affect the project, with coverage derived rather than asserted, and the release path refuses to publish while an advisory in the SBOM is undecided. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/docs/dependency-track.md
osps_vm_05_01_justification: deny.toml defines the thresholds: licence allowlist, wildcard bans, registry and git source restrictions, and reasoned skips; lint:deny runs it in the gate and audit:deny checks the RustSec feed weekly. https://github.com/monumental-archive/iiif-server/blob/main/deny.toml
osps_vm_05_02_justification: The policy is enforced at the release boundary, not merely stated: the release path refuses to publish with an undecided advisory in its SBOM. It has already blocked a real release in the lab rather than being theoretical. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/docs/dependency-track.md
osps_vm_05_03_justification: Automatically on every change: cargo-deny (deny.toml) in the gate and dependency-review on every pull request; Renovate raises security updates as advisories land. https://github.com/monumental-archive/iiif-server/blob/main/.github/workflows/dependency-review.yml
osps_vm_06_01_justification: SECURITY.md section 'Static analysis policy' defines the remediation threshold, and it is zero: any SAST finding - CodeQL, the lint belt, zizmor and peers - fails the CI gate, and a red gate cannot merge, so findings are remediated or explicitly and reviewably suppressed with a written reason before the change lands. There is no severity triage queue for static findings because there is no state in which one is outstanding on a default branch. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/SECURITY.md
osps_vm_06_02_justification: Every change is evaluated and blocked on violation: CodeQL (Rust and Actions) runs on this repository, and clippy at every group with -D warnings, cargo-deny and zizmor run in the gate, a required check. https://github.com/monumental-archive/iiif-server/blob/main/.github/workflows/ci.yml
access_continuity_justification: docs/continuity.md is exactly this document: assets and their recovery paths, a break-glass procedure for the tag-minting App, a succession plan, and an explicit list of deliberate single points of failure. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/docs/continuity.md
accessibility_best_practices_justificati: The project has no bespoke website: documentation is plain Markdown rendered by GitHub, which is keyboard-navigable and screen-reader friendly, and the content is text with descriptive link text rather than images carrying meaning.
assurance_case_justification: docs/assurance-case.md is the assurance case: threat model, trust boundaries, secure design principles, common implementation weaknesses countered, and why it is believed sufficient. https://github.com/monumental-archive/iiif-server/blob/main/docs/assurance-case.md
automated_integration_testing_justificat: The gate (.github/workflows/ci.yml, calling the org's shared gate) runs `mise run ci` - including `cargo test --workspace --all-features --locked` - on every push to main, every pull request and every merge-queue run, and reports as a required check. https://github.com/monumental-archive/iiif-server/blob/main/.github/workflows/ci.yml
build_common_tools_justification: cargo and rustc, the standard Rust build tools, at the version pinned in mise.toml; mise installs them. https://github.com/monumental-archive/iiif-server/blob/main/mise.toml
build_floss_tools_justification: The build needs only FLOSS tools: rustc and cargo (MIT/Apache-2.0), cargo-auditable, and mise to pin them. https://github.com/monumental-archive/iiif-server/blob/main/mise.toml
build_non_recursive_justification: cargo builds the whole workspace from one manifest graph (Cargo.toml lists the members); there is no recursive make or subdirectory build. https://github.com/monumental-archive/iiif-server/blob/main/Cargo.toml
build_preserve_debug_justification: Cargo.toml defines no profile that strips symbols: a plain `cargo build` produces the dev profile with full debug information, and a release build keeps it with CARGO_PROFILE_RELEASE_DEBUG=true, cargo's standard override. https://github.com/monumental-archive/iiif-server/blob/main/Cargo.toml
build_repeatable_justification: Building is verified bit for bit on every release. The oci-image class builds the image per architecture twice, independently ('Build image' and 'Rebuild image (repro)'), and the 'Repro gate' job compares them before anything is signed or published; a mismatch fails the release. Verified on the v0.2.3 publish run: https://github.com/monumental-archive/iiif-server/actions/runs/43594602252
build_reproducible_justification: Reproducibility is proven on every release, not asserted: the publish workflow rebuilds the image for each architecture independently and its repro gate compares the outputs bit for bit before signing (v0.2.3: https://github.com/monumental-archive/iiif-server/actions/runs/43594602252). CLAUDE.md records why the binary is built natively and only COPYed into a pure-assembly Dockerfile: the in-container build was measured nondeterministic. https://github.com/monumental-archive/iiif-server/blob/main/CLAUDE.md
build_standard_variables_justification: cargo honours the Rust build's standard variables (RUSTFLAGS, CARGO_TARGET_DIR, CARGO_PROFILE_*), and the one dependency that compiles C/assembly (ring, via the cc crate) honours CC, CFLAGS and AR. The project's own code is pure Rust and adds no build script that overrides them. https://github.com/monumental-archive/iiif-server/blob/main/Cargo.toml
build_justification: The software is Rust and requires building; the build system is cargo over the workspace in Cargo.toml (crates/core, crates/sources, crates/server), with the toolchain pinned in mise.toml. The release builds the shipped binary from the `binary-crate: crates/server` declaration in .github/workflows/publish.yml. https://github.com/monumental-archive/iiif-server/blob/main/Cargo.toml
bus_factor_justification: The bus factor is 1 — a single maintainer. Recorded plainly in docs/slsa-reference.md as headcount-blocked, with docs/continuity.md carrying the succession and break-glass paths that exist precisely because of it. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/docs/continuity.md
code_of_conduct_justification: The org CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md is served to this repository as a default community health file (README.md says so). https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md
code_review_standards_justification: GOVERNANCE.md section 'Code review' documents how review is conducted and what must be checked: that the change does what it says, that the claim it makes is one its checks actually enforce, that it does not weaken a documented control, and that documentation changed alongside behaviour - with the mechanical floor (formatting, linting, licence headers, commit shape, tests) left to the CI gate rather than the reviewer. What is required to be acceptable is stated too: a green gate, resolved review threads enforced by ruleset, a DCO sign-off on every commit, and a PR title and body fit to become the permanent squash commit. It also records that with one maintainer there is no second human reviewer, and names the gate as the compensating control. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md#code-review
coding_standards_enforced_justification: Automatically, in the gate on every pull request: rustfmt, clippy -D warnings, rustdoc -D warnings, typos, rumdl, taplo and the commit-shape and DCO checks; `mise run fix` applies the machine-fixable subset. https://github.com/monumental-archive/iiif-server/blob/main/mise.toml
coding_standards_justification: The coding standard is executable: rustfmt and clippy at every group including restriction, the workspace lint table in Cargo.toml, rustdoc with warnings as errors, and Conventional Commits; CLAUDE.md 'Ground rules' states the exception mechanism (#[expect] with a reason, nothing else). https://github.com/monumental-archive/iiif-server/blob/main/CLAUDE.md
contribution_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md documents the process explicitly: fork/branch, conventional imperative commit subjects under 72 columns enforced by committed, DCO sign-off, `mise run ci` green locally, pull request, squash merge. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
contribution_requirements_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md's 'Requirements for acceptable contributions' section: every change arrives by pull request, must pass `mise run ci` (the coding standard in executable form), uses Conventional Commits with imperative lowercase subjects, and is squash-merged. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
contributors_unassociated_justification: There is one significant contributor, so there cannot be two unassociated ones. Headcount, not policy: contributions are welcomed under CONTRIBUTING.md. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
copyright_per_file_justification: Every Rust and shell file carries an SPDX copyright header, and REUSE.toml covers every other file; lint:reuse enforces it and api.reuse.software reports the repository compliant. https://github.com/monumental-archive/iiif-server/blob/main/REUSE.toml
crypto_algorithm_agility_justification: The project selects no algorithms itself; outbound TLS uses rustls, which negotiates among several TLS 1.2/1.3 cipher suites, so a broken suite is dropped by a dependency update without code changes here.
crypto_call_justification: Cryptography is delegated to rustls and ring (TLS) and object_store (SigV4 request signing); nothing is reimplemented here. https://github.com/monumental-archive/iiif-server/blob/main/crates/sources/Cargo.toml
crypto_certificate_verification_justific: The only TLS the software performs is outbound, to S3-compatible object stores (crates/sources): reqwest over rustls with the ring provider, which verifies certificates by default. Nothing in the tree disables verification (no danger/insecure verifier). The image ships a CA bundle for this (docs/deployment.md). https://github.com/monumental-archive/iiif-server/blob/main/crates/sources/Cargo.toml
crypto_credential_agility_justification: The only credentials are object-store keys, read from the standard AWS environment variables (AmazonS3Builder::from_env), never from a project configuration file; the software stores no private keys. https://github.com/monumental-archive/iiif-server/blob/main/crates/sources/src/lib.rs
crypto_floss_justification: rustls, ring and object_store are FLOSS (Apache-2.0/MIT/ISC); cargo-deny enforces permissive licences across the tree. https://github.com/monumental-archive/iiif-server/blob/main/deny.toml
crypto_keylength_justification: The project selects no key lengths; TLS key exchange and certificates are negotiated by rustls and the remote store.
crypto_password_storage_justification: The software stores no passwords and authenticates no users; access control is delegated to a proxy (docs/deployment.md).
crypto_pfs_justification: Outbound TLS uses rustls, whose cipher suites all use ephemeral (EC)DHE key exchange, so every session has perfect forward secrecy.
crypto_published_justification: Only published, reviewed protocols are used: TLS 1.2/1.3 via rustls and AWS SigV4 (HMAC-SHA256) via object_store; nothing is invented here.
crypto_random_justification: The project generates no keys itself; rustls generates TLS keys and nonces with ring's operating-system CSPRNG.
crypto_tls12_justification: Outbound TLS uses rustls 0.23, which supports only TLS 1.2 and 1.3. The server's own listener speaks plain HTTP by design; TLS is terminated by a reverse proxy or CDN in front of it (docs/deployment.md, 'TLS + caching'). https://github.com/monumental-archive/iiif-server/blob/main/docs/deployment.md
crypto_used_network_justification: The software carries no authentication or other security mechanism over its own listener (no auth, no TLS by design, docs/deployment.md); those are layered in front of it at the proxy. The one credential-bearing connection, to the object store, uses AWS SigV4 (the secret key is never transmitted) over HTTPS by default; a plain-http endpoint is honoured only when an operator configures one, for local stores such as MinIO. https://github.com/monumental-archive/iiif-server/blob/main/docs/deployment.md
crypto_verification_private_justificatio: rustls completes certificate verification during the TLS handshake, before any HTTP request (and its SigV4 Authorization header) is sent to the object store. The server sends no cookies or other private headers. https://github.com/monumental-archive/iiif-server/blob/main/crates/sources/src/lib.rs
crypto_weaknesses_justification: No broken algorithm is relied on for security: TLS via rustls (AEAD cipher suites only) and HMAC-SHA256 for SigV4. object_store links md-5 only for S3 content checksums, and ETags use SipHash for cache identity; neither is a security mechanism.
crypto_working_justification: No broken algorithm is depended on for security: rustls offers no broken suites and request signing is HMAC-SHA256.
dco_justification: Developer Certificate of Origin 1.1. Every commit must carry Signed-off-by; the commit-msg hook catches it locally and lint:dco enforces it in the gate, with no exemption list — the release commit and Renovate sign off too. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
delivery_mitm_justification: The image is delivered over HTTPS by GHCR and verified by digest and signed provenance (docs/deployment.md); deployments pin a digest. https://github.com/monumental-archive/iiif-server/blob/main/docs/deployment.md
delivery_unsigned_justification: Integrity is not fetched over http at use time: deployments pin the image digest, and checksums.txt and the Sigstore bundle are verified against a signature, not a plain download.
dependency_monitoring_justification: Renovate (renovate.json) opens updates and security updates as advisories land (v0.2.3 shipped several marked [security]); dependency-review runs on every pull request (.github/workflows/dependency-review.yml); cargo-deny checks the lockfile against deny.toml in the gate and against the RustSec advisory feed on the Monday audit (audit:deny). https://github.com/monumental-archive/iiif-server/blob/main/deny.toml
description_good_justification: README.md opens with what the software does: a complete implementation of the IIIF Image API 3.0 and 2.1, level 2 plus every optional feature, as one static pure-Rust binary. https://github.com/monumental-archive/iiif-server/blob/main/README.md
discussion_justification: GitHub Issues and pull requests: searchable, addressable by URL, open to anyone, and public. https://github.com/monumental-archive/iiif-server/issues
documentation_achievements_justification: README.md carries the generated badge block linking each achievement: CI, OpenSSF Scorecard, the three SLSA track levels, REUSE, licence, coverage, release and image size. It is rendered from the repository's facts by fix:badges and lint:badges fails the gate on drift. https://github.com/monumental-archive/iiif-server/blob/main/README.md
documentation_architecture_justification: CLAUDE.md 'Architecture' describes the three crates and their seams (grammar, evaluation, decode-transform-encode pipeline, Source abstraction, HTTP layer); docs/design-spec.md is the founding design and docs/assurance-case.md draws the trust boundaries. https://github.com/monumental-archive/iiif-server/blob/main/docs/design-spec.md
documentation_basics_justification: README.md (what ships, running it, building it), docs/deployment.md (container, verification, TLS and caching, access control, systemd), MAINTENANCE.md (support policy and versioning) and docs/roadmap.md. https://github.com/monumental-archive/iiif-server/tree/main/docs
documentation_current_justification: Documentation changes in the same pull request as behaviour; lint:docs builds rustdoc with warnings as errors and runs the doc tests in the gate, lint:badges keeps the README badge block derived, and the Monday audit checks link liveness (audit:links, 134 of 134 OK on the last run). https://github.com/monumental-archive/iiif-server/blob/main/mise.toml
documentation_interface_justification: The external interface is the IIIF Image API (specified by iiif.io; the compliance table and endpoints are in README.md), the CLI (serve, check, healthcheck) and the container contract, all documented in README.md and docs/deployment.md; MAINTENANCE.md states which of them semver covers. https://github.com/monumental-archive/iiif-server/blob/main/docs/deployment.md
documentation_quick_start_justification: README.md opens with one `docker run` line that serves a directory of masters, and docs/deployment.md gives the compose, S3 and systemd variants. https://github.com/monumental-archive/iiif-server/blob/main/README.md
documentation_roadmap_justification: docs/roadmap.md states what the project intends to do and not do over the next year; the feature surface is frozen with pre-refusals in MAINTENANCE.md and docs/design-spec.md. https://github.com/monumental-archive/iiif-server/blob/main/docs/roadmap.md
documentation_security_justification: docs/assurance-case.md states the threat model, trust boundaries and the security property claimed, and MAINTENANCE.md 'The security property' and 'What is NOT claimed' state what users may and may not expect (no TLS or authentication in the engine by design). https://github.com/monumental-archive/iiif-server/blob/main/docs/assurance-case.md
dynamic_analysis_enable_assertions_justi: The fuzz run uses `cargo fuzz run --careful`, which rebuilds std with debug assertions and extra UB checks, and cargo-fuzz builds with debug assertions and overflow checks on; the test suite runs in cargo's dev profile, where debug_assert! and integer-overflow checks are enabled. https://github.com/monumental-archive/iiif-server/actions/runs/43542858673
dynamic_analysis_fixed_justification: Findings are fixed before release: fuzzing found a 25 GB decompression bomb and two upstream decoder bugs, all fixed (the bomb is now a committed regression fixture, tests/fixtures/bomb_declared_512x16777335.png), recorded in docs/session-report-2026-07-26.md. https://github.com/monumental-archive/iiif-server/blob/main/docs/session-report-2026-07-26.md
dynamic_analysis_justification: Four cargo-fuzz targets (fuzz/fuzz_targets: url_grammar, v2_grammar, identifier, master_open) run for 300 s each under AddressSanitizer on the Monday audit (audit:fuzz), and lint:fuzz-build compiles them in the gate. The last run executed 3.6M-24.8M inputs per target: https://github.com/monumental-archive/iiif-server/actions/runs/43542858673 . Property tests (proptest) also vary inputs over the URL grammar in every gate run.
dynamic_analysis_unsafe_justification: The workspace is `unsafe_code = forbid` (Cargo.toml), but dependencies contain unsafe Rust and ring contains C/assembly, so the fuzz targets run under AddressSanitizer every week to detect memory-safety errors: https://github.com/monumental-archive/iiif-server/actions/runs/43542858673
english_justification: All documentation, code comments, issues and commit messages are in English.
enhancement_responses_justification: Enhancement requests are answered in advance as well as case by case: MAINTENANCE.md 'Pre-refusals' declines named features with reasons, and every issue in the tracker has a maintainer response (no open issue is unanswered). https://github.com/monumental-archive/iiif-server/blob/main/MAINTENANCE.md
external_dependencies_justification: Machine-readable and locked: Cargo.toml and Cargo.lock (every build is --locked), fuzz/Cargo.lock for the fuzz workspace, mise.toml and mise.lock for toolchains, and digest-pinned base images in the Dockerfile. https://github.com/monumental-archive/iiif-server/blob/main/Cargo.lock
floss_license_justification: Released under AGPL-3.0-only, a FLOSS licence; Cargo.toml declares it and REUSE.toml applies it to every file. https://github.com/monumental-archive/iiif-server/blob/main/LICENSE
governance_justification: GOVERNANCE.md documents the decision model explicitly rather than aspirationally: one maintainer deciding in the open, significant decisions made in writing and in public before they are implemented (the docs-first standup, recorded as issues and pull requests), declined paths recorded with reasons so they are re-litigated against the record, and a written succession plan. It is served from the organisation's .github repository as a default community health file, so it governs every repository that does not carry its own. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md
hardened_site_justification: The project site is the GitHub repository. Checked against the live URL on 2026-11-15: strict-transport-security max-age=31536000; includeSubdomains; preload, a content-security-policy with default-src 'none', x-frame-options deny and x-content-type-options nosniff. https://github.com/monumental-archive/iiif-server
hardening_justification: Hardening is in the product: the workspace forbids unsafe code; the image is FROM scratch with one static binary and a CA bundle, no shell or package manager, run as non-root user 65532 (Dockerfile); decode is bounded by resource ceilings and a bounded pool with 503 backpressure; docs/deployment.md ships a hardened compose file. https://github.com/monumental-archive/iiif-server/blob/main/docs/release-engineering.md
implement_secure_design_justification: docs/assurance-case.md 'Secure design principles' walks each principle against the code: memory-safe parsing of every untrusted byte (no C parses input), least privilege (read-only root, non-root scratch image), fail-safe resource ceilings, and economy of mechanism (stateless, no auth or TLS in the engine). https://github.com/monumental-archive/iiif-server/blob/main/docs/assurance-case.md
input_validation_justification: Every untrusted input is parsed by an allowlist grammar before use: the IIIF URL grammar (crates/core/src/grammar.rs, property-tested for round-trips and totality and fuzzed), identifier handling (ident.rs, fuzzed), and master files decoded in pure Rust under resource ceilings (fuzzed under ASan). https://github.com/monumental-archive/iiif-server/blob/main/crates/core/src/grammar.rs
installation_common_justification: Installation is the standard container convention: `docker run ghcr.io/monumental-archive/iiif-server` or a digest-pinned compose service, documented in README.md and docs/deployment.md. https://github.com/monumental-archive/iiif-server/blob/main/docs/deployment.md
installation_development_quick_justifica: README.md 'Building and developing': `mise install && mise run hooks:install` installs the pinned toolchain from the lockfile, and `mise run ci` runs exactly what CI runs. https://github.com/monumental-archive/iiif-server/blob/main/README.md
installation_standard_variables_justific: There is no installation system that writes files: the only distribution is the container image (README.md, 'The image is the whole distribution'), so there is no DESTDIR-style location to honour. https://github.com/monumental-archive/iiif-server/blob/main/README.md
interact_justification: README.md explains how to contribute, get support and report security issues via the org health files (CONTRIBUTING, SUPPORT, SECURITY) served to this repository, and links the issue tracker. https://github.com/monumental-archive/iiif-server/blob/main/README.md
interfaces_current_justification: Dependencies are held current by Renovate, and use of deprecated APIs fails the build: rustc's `deprecated` lint is denied by `-D warnings` in the org's clippy run. https://github.com/monumental-archive/iiif-server/blob/main/renovate.json
internationalization_justification: The software is an HTTP image server with no user interface: it returns images and IIIF JSON, and its only text is operator diagnostics.
know_common_errors_justification: docs/assurance-case.md 'Common implementation weaknesses, countered' lists the error classes for this software (memory corruption, crashes on hostile input, parser differentials between API versions, path traversal, decompression bombs, vulnerable dependencies, workflow injection) and how each is countered. https://github.com/monumental-archive/iiif-server/blob/main/docs/assurance-case.md
know_secure_design_justification: The maintainer wrote docs/assurance-case.md 'Secure design principles', applying them to this design: memory-safe parsing of untrusted bytes, least privilege, fail-safe defaults and economy of mechanism. https://github.com/monumental-archive/iiif-server/blob/main/docs/assurance-case.md
license_location_justification: LICENSE at the repository root and LICENSES/AGPL-3.0-only.txt; api.reuse.software reports the repository compliant. https://github.com/monumental-archive/iiif-server/blob/main/LICENSE
license_per_file_justification: Every Rust and shell file carries an SPDX-License-Identifier header (AGPL-3.0-only) and REUSE.toml covers the rest; lint:reuse enforces it. https://github.com/monumental-archive/iiif-server/blob/main/REUSE.toml
maintained_justification: Actively maintained: v0.2.3 released 2026-11-14, Renovate keeps dependencies current, and the Monday audit runs fuzzing, the validators and the advisory feed. https://github.com/monumental-archive/iiif-server/releases
maintenance_or_update_justification: MAINTENANCE.md states what a version promises, the tag policy (immutable versions, floating 0.x tags, digest pinning for deployments) and the response window, so users can update between versions safely. https://github.com/monumental-archive/iiif-server/blob/main/MAINTENANCE.md
no_leaked_credentials_justification: No credential is committed. GitHub secret scanning with push protection is enforced by the organisation security configuration, trivy's secret rules run in the gate, and the design avoids long-lived credentials entirely: publishing is keyless via trusted publishing and OIDC.
regression_tests_added50_justification: Not measured, so not claimed. Some fixes did ship their regression case (the decompression bomb fixture; #39 with its HTTP test), but no one has classified every fix commit in the window.
release_notes_justification: Every release carries notes: CHANGELOG.md is generated from conventional commits by the org release workflow and the same section is attached to the GitHub release. https://github.com/monumental-archive/iiif-server/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md
release_notes_vulns_justification: v0.2.3 fixed known vulnerabilities in dependencies and its notes identify them: each such entry is marked [security] (rustls, tokio) and links the pull request that names the advisory (e.g. GHSA-2mjx-qc3c-rqvc / RUSTSEC-2026-0285 in #149). No vulnerability in the project's own code has been published. https://github.com/monumental-archive/iiif-server/releases/tag/v0.2.3
repo_interim_justification: Every change lands as a pull request with its own commits; the repository contains the full development history, not only released states.
repo_track_justification: Git records author, committer, timestamp and diff for every change; history is protected by org rulesets and every revision carries a signed source-provenance attestation (SLSA Source L3).
report_archive_justification: The issue tracker is public and searchable. https://github.com/monumental-archive/iiif-server/issues?q=is%3Aissue
report_process_justification: Bug reports go to GitHub Issues using the org's issue forms; SUPPORT.md (org health file) states where to ask. https://github.com/monumental-archive/iiif-server/issues/new/choose
report_responses_justification: Every issue in the tracker has a maintainer response or was closed by the pull request that resolved it; none is open without a response.
require_2FA_justification: Two-factor authentication is required organisation-wide — GitHub reports two_factor_requirement_enabled for the monumental-archive organisation — so it covers pushing to the repository and access to private vulnerability reports alike.
roles_responsibilities_justification: GOVERNANCE.md carries a 'Roles and responsibilities' table naming three roles - maintainer/owner, contributor, automation - and what each is responsible for. Who holds the maintainer role is unambiguous: the @monumental-archive/owners team, which CODEOWNERS routes every review to in every repository, and joining that team is what becoming a maintainer concretely means. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md#roles-and-responsibilities
secure_2FA_justification: The 2FA in use is cryptographic rather than SMS-based: GitHub's supported second factors here are TOTP and WebAuthn, and the organisation's requirement is satisfied without SMS.
security_review_justification: docs/assurance-case.md is a security review against this server's own requirements and boundaries, kept current with the code (it states what remains and why it is believed sufficient). https://github.com/monumental-archive/iiif-server/blob/main/docs/assurance-case.md
signed_releases_justification: Verified on v0.2.3: the release carries attestations.intoto.jsonl (Sigstore evidence bundle) and checksums.txt, and the image is signed keylessly with build provenance by the org signer. docs/deployment.md 'Verifying what you pulled' gives the verification command. https://github.com/monumental-archive/iiif-server/releases/tag/v0.2.3
sites_https_justification: The repository, its releases and its documentation are served by GitHub over HTTPS; there is no separate project website.
sites_password_security_justification: The project sites are GitHub; the project stores no passwords of its own.
small_tasks_justification: No open issue in this repository is labelled good first issue or help wanted today. https://github.com/monumental-archive/iiif-server/issues
static_analysis_common_vulnerabilities_j: CodeQL's Rust security queries run on this repository, cargo-deny checks the RustSec vulnerability database, and clippy runs at every group including restriction (unwrap_used and expect_used are named in Cargo.toml) to target the panic classes.
static_analysis_fixed_justification: Findings are fixed before merge: the gate blocks a pull request on any clippy, cargo-deny or zizmor finding, so none reaches main unaddressed.
static_analysis_often_justification: On every commit: the gate runs on every pull request, push to main and merge-queue run, and CodeQL runs on pushes and pull requests.
static_analysis_justification: CodeQL (Rust and Actions) runs on this repository, and the gate runs clippy at every group including restriction with -D warnings, cargo-deny, zizmor and actionlint on every pull request, before any release. https://github.com/monumental-archive/iiif-server/blob/main/.github/workflows/ci.yml
test_branch_coverage80_justification: Branch coverage is not measured; only statement coverage is (74.1%, .coverage-floor), which is itself below 80%. https://github.com/monumental-archive/iiif-server/blob/main/.coverage-floor
test_continuous_integration_justificatio: .github/workflows/ci.yml runs the full gate, including the test suite, on every push and pull request to main and in the merge queue. https://github.com/monumental-archive/iiif-server/blob/main/.github/workflows/ci.yml
test_invocation_justification: `mise run test` (cargo test --workspace --all-features --locked), or `mise run ci` for the whole gate; documented in README.md and CLAUDE.md. https://github.com/monumental-archive/iiif-server/blob/main/mise.toml
test_most_justification: Statement coverage is measured with cargo-llvm-cov at 74.1% (.coverage-floor, ratcheted by coverage:check in the gate), plus property tests over the grammar, golden/differential pixel tests and HTTP-semantics tests. https://github.com/monumental-archive/iiif-server/blob/main/.coverage-floor
test_policy_mandated_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md, 'Requirements for acceptable contributions' item 3, is the formal written policy: a change that adds or changes behaviour adds the check that holds it - a test that fails without the change where a test suite exists, and a lint, audit task or workflow assertion in configuration and policy repositories. It is stated as policy: the gate's checks are the specification, and functionality nothing enforces is functionality the next change may silently remove. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
test_policy_justification: The org CONTRIBUTING.md item 3 requires a change that adds behaviour to add the check that holds it, and this repository's CLAUDE.md adds that new work slots into its validator, golden/differential and property-test harnesses and that correctness fixes want a failing test first. https://github.com/monumental-archive/iiif-server/blob/main/CLAUDE.md
test_statement_coverage80_justification: Measured statement coverage is 74.1% (.coverage-floor, derived at v0.2.3), below 80%. The ratchet only rises. https://github.com/monumental-archive/iiif-server/blob/main/.coverage-floor
test_justification: A FLOSS automated suite: `cargo test --workspace --all-features --locked` (mise run test) over crates/core/tests and crates/server/tests plus unit and doc tests, run in CI by the gate. https://github.com/monumental-archive/iiif-server/blob/main/mise.toml
tests_are_added_justification: Major functionality shipped with its tests: the v2.1 endpoint with both official validators (M3), HTTP caching with http_semantics.rs (M5), object-store serving with a pixel-verified end-to-end (M4), and fuzzing with the decompression-bomb fixture (M7). https://github.com/monumental-archive/iiif-server/tree/main/crates/core/tests
tests_documented_added_justification: The policy is stated in the documented instructions for change proposals themselves: CONTRIBUTING.md, item 3 of 'Requirements for acceptable contributions' - a change that adds or changes behaviour adds the check that holds it, and a bug fix adds the case that reproduced the bug. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
two_person_review_justification: With a single maintainer, no proposed modification is reviewed by a person other than its author. This is the Source L4 and Gold boundary for this project and is recorded as headcount-blocked in docs/slsa-reference.md; it is watched as an issue rather than papered over. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/docs/slsa-reference.md
updateable_reused_components_justificati: Reused components are cargo crates at exact versions in Cargo.lock and digest-pinned base images in the Dockerfile; updating is a Renovate pull request the gate verifies. https://github.com/monumental-archive/iiif-server/blob/main/renovate.json
version_semver_justification: Semantic Versioning over a stated surface (HTTP, CLI flags, container contract), written in MAINTENANCE.md 'What a version number promises'. https://github.com/monumental-archive/iiif-server/blob/main/MAINTENANCE.md
version_tags_signed_justification: Release tags are annotated tag objects signed keylessly (Sigstore) by the release workflow. Checked on v0.2.3: GitHub reports the tag object signed with reason no_user, which means the signer is a workflow identity, not an account. https://github.com/monumental-archive/iiif-server/releases/tag/v0.2.3
version_tags_justification: Each release is an immutable v* tag minted by the release App. https://github.com/monumental-archive/iiif-server/tags
version_unique_justification: Each release has a unique version from Cargo.toml and a matching immutable v* tag. https://github.com/monumental-archive/iiif-server/releases
vulnerabilities_critical_fixed_justifica: Critical vulnerabilities are fixed as soon as they are known; Renovate raises security updates and the release refuses an undecided advisory.
vulnerabilities_fixed_60_days_justificat: There are no known unpatched medium or higher vulnerabilities: Cargo.lock on main and in v0.2.3 pins rustls 0.23.46, which carries the fixes for the 2026 rustls advisories, and cargo-deny checks the RustSec feed weekly. https://github.com/monumental-archive/iiif-server/blob/main/Cargo.lock
vulnerability_report_credit_justificatio: No vulnerability report has been resolved in the last 12 months, so there is no reporter to credit. The org SECURITY.md commits to crediting reporters.
vulnerability_report_private_justificati: GitHub private vulnerability reporting is enabled and is the documented channel in SECURITY.md, so reports stay private until an advisory is published. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/SECURITY.md
vulnerability_report_process_justificati: SECURITY.md publishes the process: private reporting through the repository's Security tab. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/SECURITY.md
vulnerability_report_response_justificat: No vulnerability report has been received in the last 6 months (this repository has no security advisories). The org SECURITY.md commits to acknowledgement within 14 days.
vulnerability_response_process_justifica: SECURITY.md documents the process end to end: private reporting through the repository's Security tab, acknowledgement within 14 days, what to expect afterwards, and the scope. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/SECURITY.md
warnings_fixed_justification: The gate fails on any compiler, clippy or rustdoc warning and no change merges red, so warnings are fixed as they appear.
warnings_justification: rustc lints are configured in Cargo.toml [workspace.lints]; clippy runs at every group including restriction with -D warnings in lint:rust, and lint:docs builds rustdoc with RUSTDOCFLAGS=-D warnings. https://github.com/monumental-archive/iiif-server/blob/main/Cargo.toml
warnings_strict_justification: Maximally strict: lint:rust runs clippy with -D warnings at every group including restriction (minus the canon's named mechanical contradictions), which denies rustc's warn-by-default lints too; exceptions are only #[expect(..., reason)]. https://github.com/monumental-archive/iiif-server/blob/main/CLAUDE.md
